reasoning_traces.think:
The emergence of locomotion in infants reflects a dual process: initial symmetric limb activity gives way to asymmetric, purposeful movement as neural centers mature past a critical threshold. This transition is governed by a threshold activation mechanism, where sensory input (floor contact) triggers motor output only after sufficient neural readiness. The sensorimotor loop then reinforces this behavior through feedback, enabling stable standing and eventual ambulation. Failure modes include delayed activation due to immature neural networks or insufficient sensory feedback, leading to prolonged dependence on external support or delayed motor milestones. These processes form a foundational basis for understanding developmental dynamics in motor control systems.
